Garmin Forerunner 265 vs Coros Pace 3: The Ultimate Running Watch Showdown (2026)

$449 Garmin Forerunner 265 vs $229 Coros Pace 3 — the two most-debated running watches on the market. One has a stunning AMOLED display and deep training metrics. The other crushes it on battery life and value. We settle the debate once and for all.

Published August 4, 2026 · Based on verified product data, spec sheets, and thousands of real user reviews

Quick Verdict

Buy the Garmin Forerunner 265 if: You want the best all-around running watch money can buy — a gorgeous AMOLED display that you can actually read in sunlight, Garmin's unrivaled training ecosystem (Training Readiness, HRV Status, Daily Suggested Workouts, Race Adaptive Planner), music storage for phone-free runs, Garmin Pay, and smart notifications. If you're a serious runner who also wants a great everyday smartwatch, the Forerunner 265 is worth every dollar of that $449 price tag.

Buy the Coros Pace 3 if: Battery life and value are your top priorities. The Coros Pace 3 lasts nearly 3x longer on GPS (38 hours vs 20 hours) and over 4x longer in smartwatch mode (17 days vs 13 days). It's lighter, it has a crisp always-on MIP display that's bright in direct sunlight, and Coros EvoLab provides genuinely useful training insights. At $229 — literally half the price — it's the best value proposition in running watches today.

Our pick: The Garmin Forerunner 265. The AMOLED display, depth of training data, music storage, and smartwatch features justify the premium for anyone who runs seriously and wants a single watch for daily wear. But if battery life is your non-negotiable, the Coros Pace 3 is an exceptional watch at an incredible price — and we wouldn't blame you for going that route.

Our Pick 🏆 Garmin Forerunner 265

$449.00 on Amazon

The Garmin Forerunner 265 is the watch that finally made the running world go all-in on AMOLED. It replaces the Forerunner 255 with a stunning 1.3-inch AMOLED display that's bright, colorful, and remains readable even under direct sunlight thanks to Garmin's excellent brightness auto-adjustment.

The AMOLED display changes the game. Previous Forerunner models used MIP (Memory-in-Pixel) displays — perfectly functional but not exactly exciting to look at. The 265's AMOLED screen makes everyday use genuinely pleasant. Maps look crisp, data screens are vibrant, and the always-on mode still delivers excellent battery life. It's the display you'll want on your wrist even when you're not running.

Training metrics are second to none. Garmin's Training Readiness score combines your sleep quality, recovery, HRV status, and training load to tell you whether you're primed for a hard workout or need an easy day. Morning Report gives you a daily briefing of sleep, recovery, training outlook, and weather as soon as you wake up. Daily Suggested Workouts adapt after every run based on your actual performance and recovery. And the Race Adaptive Planner — input a race and course into Garmin Connect, and the watch builds a personalized training plan around it.

Music storage and smart features set it apart. Store up to 500 songs from Spotify, Amazon Music, or Apple Music and run without your phone. Garmin Pay handles contactless payments. Smart notifications keep you connected. These are features the Coros Pace 3 either lacks entirely or implements in a more limited way.

Key specs: 1.3" AMOLED (416×416), multi-band GNSS with SatIQ, Elevate v4 heart rate sensor, Pulse Ox, 30+ activity profiles, music storage, Garmin Pay, 13 days smartwatch / 20 hours GPS, 5 ATM water rating, 47g case weight.

⏱️ Coros Pace 3

$229.00 on Amazon

Coros came out of nowhere a few years ago and disrupted the running watch market. The Pace 3 is their latest flagship for runners, and it's a masterclass in prioritizing what matters most: battery life, GPS accuracy, and weight — all at an aggressive price point.

The battery life is absurdly good. 38 hours of continuous GPS tracking with all-systems GNSS enabled. In standard GPS mode, you get up to 56 hours. In smartwatch mode, 17 days. This means you can run a 100-mile ultra marathon, track every mile, and still have battery left for daily wear. The Garmin Forerunner 265 gives you 20 hours of GPS. That's still good — but the Coros is in another league entirely for endurance athletes.

The MIP display is a feature, not a compromise. Coros stuck with a 1.2-inch always-on MIP (Memory-in-Pixel) display. It's not as vibrant as AMOLED, but it's perfectly readable in direct sunlight, uses negligible power, and never requires a wrist-flick gesture to turn on. For runners who spend hours outdoors, the MIP display is genuinely better in bright conditions. The trade-off is that indoors and in low light, it's less vibrant than the Garmin's screen.

EvoLab is genuinely impressive. Coros's training platform tracks your VO2 max, training load, recovery time, and performance metrics. The training plans are solid, and the metrics are backed by Coros's growing sports science team. It's not quite as deep as Garmin's ecosystem — especially when you factor in Garmin Connect's social features, challenges, and third-party integrations — but for most runners, it's more than enough.

It's incredibly light. At just 30 grams (without strap), the Pace 3 is 17 grams lighter than the Forerunner 265. That's a 36% weight reduction. For runners who care about every gram on their wrist — especially during races — this difference is noticeable.

Key specs: 1.2" always-on MIP display, multi-band GNSS, optical HR + SpO2, Coros EvoLab, touchscreen + digital dial, 17 days smartwatch / 38 hours GPS, 5 ATM water rating, 30g case weight, no music storage, limited contactless payments.

The Display Debate: AMOLED vs MIP

This is the single biggest philosophical difference between the two watches, and it largely determines which camp you'll fall into.

AMOLED — the Garmin advantage. The Forerunner 265's AMOLED display is objectively more beautiful. Colors pop, blacks are true black, and the interface feels modern and premium. With automatic brightness adjustment, it's perfectly readable outdoors. Indoor use and low-light viewing are excellent. The trade-off? AMOLED uses more power, especially with the always-on mode enabled. Garmin has done impressive battery optimization — 13 days of smartwatch use and 20 hours of GPS tracking is respectable — but it can't match the endurance of a MIP display.

MIP — the Coros advantage. The Pace 3's MIP display reflects ambient light, meaning the brighter the sun, the better it looks. It's always on with zero battery penalty. For ultra runners, triathletes, and anyone who spends 5+ hours at a time on the trails, MIP is the honest choice. It also enables the Pace 3's extraordinary 38-hour GPS battery life. The downside? Indoors and in low light, the MIP display looks muted compared to AMOLED. Colors are flat. It's functional, not flashy.

"The Garmin Forerunner 265 is the watch you'll enjoy looking at. The Coros Pace 3 is the watch you'll forget you're wearing."

Training Metrics: Depth vs. Focus

Garmin wins on depth. The Forerunner 265 offers training features that no other watch at any price matches. Training Readiness combines sleep, HRV, recovery, and training load into a single score that tells you if today's a hard day or an easy day. HRV Status tracks your heart rate variability overnight and alerts you to changes that could indicate overtraining or illness. The Race Adaptive Planner builds a training plan around a specific race and course. And Daily Suggested Workouts adapt after every single run based on your actual performance and recovery state. This is a watch that gets smarter the more you use it.

Coros EvoLab is leaner but effective. Coros's training platform tracks VO2 max, training load, recovery time, and provides structured workout plans. It's clean, accurate, and built around the core metrics that most runners actually use. What it lacks is the breadth of Garmin's ecosystem — no Body Battery, no Stress Score, no sophisticated HRV analysis, no adaptive workout suggestions that change based on daily readiness. For most runners, EvoLab covers the essentials. For data nerds, Garmin is the clear winner.

Battery: It's Not Even Close

The Coros Pace 3 obliterates the Garmin on battery life. 38 hours of all-systems GPS tracking vs 20 hours. 17 days of smartwatch use vs 13 days. The gap widens further in standard GPS mode — 56 hours for the Coros vs 24 hours for the Garmin.

For context: a 100-mile ultra runner will comfortably finish with the Coros Pace 3 tracking every second. With the Garmin Forerunner 265, you'd need to bring a charging cable or use power-saving modes that reduce tracking accuracy.

For the everyday runner doing 30-60 minute runs, both watches will go weeks between charges. But if you run marathons, ultras, or multi-day adventure races, the Coros Pace 3's battery advantage is the single most important spec on this entire comparison table.

Smart Features: Garmin Pulls Ahead

Music storage is the biggest differentiator. The Garmin Forerunner 265 stores up to 500 songs from Spotify, Amazon Music, or Apple Music and plays them through Bluetooth headphones — completely phone-free. The Coros Pace 3 has no onboard music storage at all. If you run without your phone, the Garmin is the only choice.

Garmin Pay works at more stores and in more countries than Coros Pay, which is still in limited rollout. Smart notifications are comparable on both watches — calls, texts, and app notifications come through reliably.

Garmin Connect is a genuinely deep ecosystem with social features (challenges, groups, segments), extensive third-party integrations (Strava, TrainingPeaks, MyFitnessPal, Komoot), and detailed analytics dashboards. Coros's app is cleaner and simpler, but it doesn't have the same breadth of integrations or community features.

The Elephant in the Room: The Price Gap

Let's be direct: the Garmin Forerunner 265 costs literally twice as much as the Coros Pace 3. At $449 vs $229, we're talking about a $220 difference.

Is the Garmin twice the watch? In raw features, it's arguable. The AMOLED display is genuinely better. The music storage is a real differentiator. Garmin's training metrics are deeper, and the ecosystem is broader. But for a runner who just wants GPS tracking, heart rate monitoring, and great battery life — the Coros Pace 3 delivers 90% of the experience for 50% of the price.

Here's how we think about it: if you run 20+ miles per week, train for specific races, and want every data advantage you can get, the Garmin Forerunner 265 is worth the premium. The training insights genuinely help you run smarter, not just harder.

If you're a newer runner, a ultra/trail runner, or someone who prioritizes value and battery life above all else, the Coros Pace 3 is arguably the better watch — and at $229, it's one of the best deals in all of wearables, period.

The Bottom Line

Our Take

The Garmin Forerunner 265 is the best all-around running watch you can buy right now. The AMOLED display is a meaningful upgrade over every previous Forerunner, the training metrics are genuinely useful (not just data for data's sake), and music storage + Garmin Pay make it a true everyday smartwatch. If you're a serious runner who also wants a watch you'll enjoy wearing all day, this is the one.

But the Coros Pace 3 is an incredible watch in its own right. The battery life is best-in-class, the weight is barely noticeable, and at $229, the value proposition is unmatched. For ultra runners, budget-conscious athletes, or anyone who wants a focused running tool without the distractions of smartwatch features, the Pace 3 is arguably the smarter buy.

Two watches. Two philosophies. Both excellent. The right choice depends on what kind of runner you are.
